text.p: Several brokers raised profit forecasts for Compagnie Bancaire on Wednesday following its buy out offers for finance house subsidiaries Cardif and UFB Locabail, on a view they will be earnings positive, fund managers said.
The buy-outs also mean Cie Bancaire will become less of a holding company, they added.
The move revived speculation over changes in the Paribas group, which owns 46.5 percent of Cie Bancaire, and helped drive up the financial sector.
"This shows that Paribas is continuing to restructure in a significant way," a fund manager said.

Among the scenarios being talked about in the market are the sale of Cie Bancaire by Paribas, a disposal of Cetelem by Cie Bancaire, which owns 61 percent of the finance house, or alternatively, a buy-out of Cetelem minority shareholders. However, some believe the latter deal would be too costly.
Cie Bancaire stock was up 6.69 percent at 734 francs on volume of 186,366 shares, at 1405 GMT, while Paribas was up 4.49 percent at 404.5, with 787,421 shares changing hands.

Cheuvreux de Virieu held its "3", or sell, recommendation on Cie Bancaire, viewing the stock as fully valued, but upped its profit forecast to 46.6 francs per share from 45 for this year, and to 54 from 52.6 for next year.

Massonaud believes the deal will enhance earnings by about five percent after write-down of goodwill over 20 years and raised its EPS forecast to 46.10 francs from 44.30 for 1997 and to 57 from 54.40 for 1998.
Massonaud thinks the buy-out has put to rest the market's speculation on a disposal of Cetelem, the jewel in the crown.
Natexis held its B1 recommendation, performance in line with the market, but also raised its profit forecast for 1997 to 43.75 from 40.7 francs.

Cie Bancaire launched a buy-out for Cardif at 900 francs per share and UFB Locabail at 600 francs. It said the offers represented a maximum investment of three billion francs and would require a two billion franc capital increase to finance.
Trading in Cardif and Locabail shares was suspended.
